summary: Haiti admits citizens of most countries visa-free for up to 90 days, collecting a USD 10 tourist fee on arrival, and CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months. Paperwork is not the obstacle here: gang violence has put the whole country, including Port-au-Prince, under do-not-travel advisories, and commercial flights are frequently suspended.

vaccinations.name: Hepatitis A, typhoid and routine vaccines
vaccinations.text: Not an entry condition, but hepatitis A and typhoid vaccination and up-to-date routine vaccines are strongly recommended for Haiti. Cholera has circulated since 2022 and water-borne illness is common; malaria is present year-round in much of the country.

travelInsurance.text: No official source states an insurance requirement for entry, but comprehensive coverage including medical evacuation is essential: Canada's travel advice says doctors and hospitals expect immediate cash payment even from insured patients. Read the policy wording carefully. Many insurers void coverage for countries under a government do-not-travel advisory, which now covers all of Haiti.

notes: The UK FCDO says penalties for possession, use or trafficking of illegal drugs are severe: suspects may be jailed for weeks or months before appearing in court. Pack your own luggage and do not carry items through customs for anyone else.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says most leading hotels accept major credit cards, but Haitian ATMs are unreliable and you should carry enough cash in case you cannot use an ATM or card. Australia's Smartraveller says US dollars are widely accepted.

safety.text: Armed gangs control much of Port-au-Prince and stretches of the main roads, and kidnapping for ransom, carjacking and roadblocks are common. The US, UK and Canada all advise against all travel to Haiti. Toussaint Louverture airport has been closed to commercial traffic for extended periods since 2024. Do not travel without professional security arrangements.

tips.text: Most governments advise against all travel to Haiti. Gangs control roads around Port-au-Prince — including the route to the airport — and foreigners have been kidnapped for ransom. Anyone traveling for work should have professional security and evacuation arrangements in place before arrival.

The Government of Canada says there are no regular international flights to or from Port-au-Prince until further notice, that flights using the airport are often targeted by gunfire, and that Cap-Haïtien's international airport is the best option. Confirm your flight's status with your airline before you travel.
The UK FCDO says tourists must pay an entry fee of 10 US dollars in cash on arrival — have it ready in US dollar notes.

The Government of Canada says prices are often quoted in 'Haitian dollars' (5 gourdes = 1 Haitian dollar) or in US dollars, although all prices should be in gourdes since March 2018. Confirm which unit a price is in before paying.

Register with your embassy before arrival and carry a charged phone with emergency contact numbers. The Government of Canada says mobile coverage may be intermittent in rural areas and roadside assistance is deficient.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Haiti?
faq.answer: Usually not. Haiti admits citizens of most countries — including the EU, UK, US, Canada and the Commonwealth — visa-free for up to 90 days, with a USD 10 tourist fee paid on arrival. CARICOM nationals get six months. Nine nationalities must obtain a visa from a Haitian mission first, applying at least a month before departure: Colombia, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Iran, Libya, Panama, Syria, Vietnam and Yemen.

faq.question: Is it safe to travel to Haiti in 2026?
faq.answer: No, and that is the central fact about visiting Haiti right now. The US, UK and Canada all advise against all travel because of gang control of Port-au-Prince and much of the country, widespread kidnapping and armed roadblocks. Visa rules are the easy part; getting in, moving around and getting out safely is not.

faq.question: How much is Haiti's tourist fee?
faq.answer: USD 10 per visitor, collected in cash on arrival from travelers entering without a visa. It is separate from any airline taxes and from the departure fee usually built into your ticket. Carry it in US dollar notes.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Haiti without a visa?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days for most nationalities, with the officer writing the actual period on your stamp. Extensions are handled by the Direction de l'Immigration et de l'Émigration in Port-au-Prince.

faq.question: Are flights to Haiti operating?
faq.answer: Barely. The Government of Canada says there are no regular international flights to or from Port-au-Prince until further notice and that Cap-Haïtien's international airport is the best option; Australia's Smartraveller says many airlines have limited or suspended Port-au-Prince flights. Confirm your flight with the airline before you travel.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Haiti?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from or transit a yellow fever risk country in tropical Africa or South America. Australia's Smartraveller adds that cholera is an ongoing risk in parts of Haiti: drink boiled or bottled water with intact seals.
